correctness.rationale: For every dyadic side length n_i, the cyclic shift module k[x_i]/(x_i^{n_i}-1) has x_i+x_i^{-1}=x_i^{-1}(x_i+1)^2 and therefore exactly two nilpotent Jordan chains of size h_i=n_i/2. After tensoring all d independent sides, the orthogonal-neighbor operator is multiplication by w=sum t_i on 2^d copies of B=k[t_i]/(t_i^{h_i}). Select maximal h_k=H and change variables t_k=w+sum others; characteristic-two Frobenius gives t_k^H=w^H since other h_i divide H. Thus A has exactly N/H copies of J_H(0). The two-layer reversible F satisfies F^2+I=diag(A,A)F, F^{2H}=I, and ker(F+I) is isomorphic to ker A; with c=N/H blocks in dimension 2N, all unipotent blocks have length L=2H. This proves exact fixed and primitive periods for all d>=3 over GF(2^f), not a finite experimental extrapolation. Independent full physical neighbor-matrix check on a 4x4x4 torus verified spatial rank 32, F order 4, and fixed dimensions 32,64,128.
residual_risks: Hypothesis all cycle lengths >=4 is necessary for the simple two-distinct-neighbor graph and ordinary XOR matrix; n=2 would double-count an edge.
All side lengths must be powers of two and field of characteristic two; no statement for mixed odd components.

originality.rationale: Martin–Odlyzko–Wolfram describes general multidimensional additive cellular automata and second-order rules, but its cited Theorem 4.8 period bound assumes circumferences prime to the characteristic, specifically excluding these dyadic hypertori. Earlier exact 1D reversible and 2D first-order cyclic cases are related and credited, but do not state the all-d two-time-level uniform Jordan similarity and complete orbit census. The polynomial change-of-variable proof supplies the substantive higher-dimensional specialization.
residual_risks: Characteristic-two module methods are classical; an earlier unindexed multidimensional specialization of the identical nilpotent uniform-block argument could cover the theorem.
